extracted.intended_audience: patent applicants, patent attorneys/agents, and other practitioners involved in U.S. patent prosecution before the USPTO
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and substantive requirements governing termination of proceedings, publication/nonpublication of U.S. patent applications, redaction and early publication options, third-party submissions and protests, service of papers, unlocatable files, and (pre-2013) statutory invention registration requests. Intended to guide applicants and third parties on compliance and timing during prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Termination of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings on an application are considered terminated by the dismissal of an appeal or the failure to timely file an appeal to the court or a civil action, except where claims stand allowed in an application or where the nature of the decision requires further action by the examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The date of termination is the date the appeal is dismissed or the date on which the time for appeal to the U.S. Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit or review by civil action expires in the absence of further appeal or review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication timing (18-month rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each U.S. national application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) and each international application in compliance with 35 U.S.C. 371 will be published promptly after the expiration of 18 months from the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought, unless specific exceptions apply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See exceptions for no-longer-pending applications, national security classification/secrecy orders, issuance as a patent in time, and valid nonpublication requests (§ 1.211(a)(1)-(4)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Categories of applications not published under § 1.211
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional applications (35 U.S.C. 111(b)) shall not be published; design applications (35 U.S.C. chapter 16), international design applications (35 U.S.C. chapter 38), and reissue applications (35 U.S.C. chapter 25) shall not be published under § 1.211.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These application types are expressly excluded from publication under § 1.211(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication prerequisites — filing fee and required documents
rubrics_metrics.description: An application filed under 35 U.S.C. 111(a) will not be published until it includes the basic filing fee and any required English translation; the Office may delay publishing until other required items (application size fee, specification in compliance with § 1.52 and abstract, drawings in compliance with § 1.84, sequence listing/Sequence Listing XML if applicable, and inventor’s oath/declaration or ADS with § 1.63(b) info) are included.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication may be delayed until all specified formal and electronic-filing-system-compliant materials are present; applicants should ensure required fees and documents are timely submitted to avoid delays.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refusal to publish for legal or offensive content
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office may refuse to publish an application, or to include a portion of an application in the patent application publication, if publication of the application or portion thereof would violate Federal or state law, or if the application or portion thereof contains offensive or disparaging material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should avoid including material that could trigger refusal under this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication fee payment timing
rubrics_metrics.description: The publication fee set forth in § 1.18(d) must be paid in each application published under this section before the patent will be granted. If subject to publication, the sum specified in the notice of allowance will include the publication fee which must be paid within three months from the date of mailing of the notice of allowance to avoid abandonment; this three-month period is not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If an application is not published under this section, any paid publication fee will be refunded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nonpublication request — filing-time requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: If the invention disclosed has not been and will not be the subject of an application filed in another country (or under a multilateral international agreement) that requires 18-month publication, the application will not be published provided: (1) a nonpublication request is submitted with the application upon filing; (2) the request states conspicuously that the application is not to be published under 35 U.S.C. 122(b); (3) the request contains a certification that the invention has not been and will not be subject to such foreign filing; and (4) the request is signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All four conditions must be satisfied for nonpublication protection; failure to follow formal signing/format can invalidate the request.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rescission of nonpublication request
rubrics_metrics.description: The applicant may rescind a nonpublication request at any time by submitting a rescission that: (1) identifies the application; (2) states conspicuously that the nonpublication request is rescinded; and (3) is signed in compliance with § 1.33(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A rescission can be filed anytime, restoring the application's exposure to publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to notify USPTO of subsequent foreign filing when nonpublication was requested
rubrics_metrics.description: If an applicant who submitted a nonpublication request subsequently files a corresponding application in another country or under a multilateral international agreement that requires 18-month publication, the applicant must notify the USPTO within 45 days after the foreign/international filing date; failure to timely notify will result in abandonment of the U.S. application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a strict 45-day notification requirement with abandonment as the consequence for failure to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent application publication basis and allowable amendments
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application publication shall be based upon the specification and drawings deposited on the filing date, as well as the application data sheet and/or inventor’s oath or declaration; the publication may also be based on substitute specifications or certain amendments (other than abstract or claims) and amendments to the abstract, claims (complete claim listing), and drawings if submitted in sufficient time to be entered into the file wrapper before technical preparations (generally begin 4 months prior to projected publication) have begun. National-stage applications may include international-stage amendments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants seeking to have amendments reflected in publication must submit them early enough — technical preparations usually start ~4 months before publication — or supply a compliant EFS copy per § 1.215(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Option to supply EFS-compliant copy for publication
rubrics_metrics.description: At applicant’s option, the patent application publication may be based upon a copy of the application (specification, drawings, ADS and/or oath/declaration) as amended, provided applicant supplies such a copy in compliance with USPTO patent electronic filing system (EFS) requirements within one month of the mailing date of the first Office communication that includes a confirmation number for the application, or fourteen months of the earliest filing date for which a benefit is sought, whichever is later.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supplying the EFS-compliant copy allows later amendments to be included in publication, but the copy must meet technical filing-system requirements and be timely.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignee information inclusion in publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent application publication will include the name of the assignee or person showing proprietary interest if that information is provided in the application data sheet in time to be entered into the Office file wrapper before technical preparations for publication have begun.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Providing assignee information in the ADS does not substitute for compliance with Part 3 recording requirements to have an assignment recorded by the Office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default publication if EFS copy noncompliant or untimely
rubrics_metrics.description: If the copy supplied pursuant to § 1.215(c) does not comply with EFS requirements, the Office will publish the application based upon the filing-date materials as provided in § 1.215(a). If the Office has not started the publication process, it may use an untimely filed copy to create the publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure EFS submissions meet technical requirements; otherwise the Office may ignore amendments for publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted publication when foreign-filed applications are less extensive
rubrics_metrics.description: If foreign-filed applications corresponding to the U.S. application are less extensive, the applicant may submit a redacted copy of the U.S. application eliminating any part or description not contained in the corresponding foreign applications; the redacted copy must be submitted within 16 months of the earliest filing date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Redaction is intended to align published content with what is in corresponding foreign filings; it is time-limited to a 16-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Redacted copy technical and title requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The redacted copy must be submitted in compliance with USPTO EFS requirements and the title of the invention in the redacted copy must correspond to the title of the application at the time of submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Noncompliant EFS redacted copies will result in publication of the full application as provided in § 1.215(a).

rubrics_metrics.name: Concurrent paper submissions required with redacted copy
rubrics_metrics.description: When submitting a redacted copy for publication the applicant must concurrently submit in paper to be filed in the application: (1) a certified copy of each corresponding foreign-filed application; (2) a translation of each foreign application not in English with a statement as to accuracy; (3) a marked-up copy showing redactions in brackets; and (4) a certification that the redacted copy eliminates only material not in any corresponding foreign-filed application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These paper materials must accompany the electronic redacted submission to substantiate and certify the scope of redactions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Additional requirements to limit public disclosure of complete file wrapper after redaction
rubrics_metrics.description: If applicant seeks to prevent release of the complete file wrapper for a redacted application, applicant must submit: copies of Office correspondence and applicant submissions showing desired redactions and second copies showing redacted material in brackets; file certain correspondence within one month of Office mailing; include the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)); and provide a certification that redactions are limited to material relevant only to parts not contained in corresponding foreign applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to meet these strict procedural and fee requirements means the Office will provide the complete file wrapper upon written request pursuant to § 1.14(c)(2).

rubrics_metrics.name: Early publication request procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications that will be published under § 1.211 may be published earlier at the applicant's request if the request is accompanied by the publication fee set forth in § 1.18(d). If applicant does not submit a compliant EFS copy per § 1.215(c), the Office will publish under § 1.215(a). No consideration is given to requests for publication on a certain date; such requests are treated as requests for publication as soon as possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early publication requires payment of the publication fee and cannot be constrained to a specific publication date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Voluntary publication/republication requirements and corrected publication
rubrics_metrics.description: Requests for publication of an application filed before (but pending on) Nov. 29, 2000, and requests for republication of an application previously published under § 1.211, must include an EFS-compliant copy and be accompanied by the publication fee and the processing fee (§ 1.17(i)); the Office will not publish and will refund the fee if noncompliant. The Office will grant a request for a corrected or revised patent application publication only when the Office makes a material mistake apparent from Office records; such requests for correction must be filed within two months from the publication date and are not extendable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Corrected republication is narrow — only for material Office mistakes and within a strict two-month window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of papers — authorized recipients and methods
rubrics_metrics.description: Service of papers must be on the attorney or agent of the party if there is one, or on the party if there is no attorney or agent. Service may be made by: (1) delivering a copy to the person; (2) leaving a copy at the usual place of business with someone in employment; (3) leaving a copy at the person's residence with someone of suitable age and discretion; (4) transmission by first class mail (date of mailing regarded as date of service); or (5) where none of the above is practicable, by notice published in the Official Gazette, if satisfactorily shown to the Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Choose an authorized method and ensure proper documentation of date and manner of service to satisfy procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proof of service requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Papers filed in the Office which are required to be served shall contain proof of service. Proof may appear on or be affixed to papers filed and shall include the date and manner of service. For personal service, proof shall also include the name of any person served, certified by the person who made service. Proof may be an acknowledgement of service or a statement signed by the attorney or agent containing the required information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain or prepare signed proof of service with the required details; lack of proof may render service defective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unlocatable file — applicant compliance options
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Office cannot locate the file of an application/patent after a reasonable search, the Office will notify the applicant/patentee and set a time period to comply. Applicant may comply by: (1) providing a copy of the applicant’s/patentee’s record of all correspondence between the Office and applicant (except U.S. patent documents), a list of such correspondence, and a statement that the copy is complete and accurate; (2) producing the applicant’s/patentee’s record for the Office to copy and providing a statement of completeness; or (3) stating that applicant/patentee does not possess any record of the correspondence. Failure to comply within the notice time will result in abandonment for pending applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respond promptly to unlocatable-file notices using one of the three specified options to avoid abandonment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submissions — permissible content and in writing
rubrics_metrics.description: A third party may submit for entry in the record any patents, published patent applications, or other printed publications of potential relevance to examination, if the submission complies with 35 U.S.C. 122(e) and § 1.290. Such submissions must be filed in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions are a limited mechanism to bring prior art to the examiner's attention; strict compliance with content and timing rules is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission timing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Any third-party submission must be filed prior to the earlier of: (1) the date a notice of allowance under § 1.311 is given or mailed, or (2) the later of (i) six months after the application is first published under § 1.211, or (ii) the date the first rejection under § 1.104 of any claim by the examiner is given or mailed during examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These deadlines are jurisdictional for entry; late submissions may not be entered or considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A third-party submission must include: (1) a document list identifying documents or portions being submitted; (2) a concise description of the asserted relevance of each item; (3) a legible copy of each item other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications; (4) an English translation of any non-English item; and (5) a statement by the submitting party (including certain attestations about duty to disclose and compliance with 35 U.S.C. 122(e)). The document list must be headed as a third-party submission under § 1.290, include the application number on each page, list U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications in a separate section, and identify items with specified bibliographic details.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Follow the required bibliographic identification formats for U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patents/published applications, and non-patent literature to avoid mismatch or rejection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Third-party submission fees and fee waiver
rubrics_metrics.description: Third-party submissions must be accompanied by the fee set forth in § 1.17(o) for every ten items or fraction thereof. The fee is not required for submissions listing three or fewer total items if accompanied by a statement by the submitting party that, to the party's knowledge after reasonable inquiry, the submission is the first and only submission under 35 U.S.C. 122(e) filed in the application by the party or a party in privity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When submitting multiple items, compute and include the appropriate fee; small submissions (<=3 items) may be fee-exempt if the required statement is provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant response to third-party submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: In the absence of a request by the Office, an applicant need not reply to a third-party submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Third-party submissions are entered into the record for examiner consideration; applicants only need to respond if the Office requests or takes action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests — filing, matching, and entry conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: A member of the public may file a protest against a pending application; it will be matched with the application if it adequately identifies the application. For entry, the protest must be served upon the applicant in accordance with § 1.248 or filed with the Office in duplicate if service is not possible; except for protests with the written consent of the applicant, protests must be filed prior to the application’s publication under § 1.211 or the date a notice of allowance under § 1.311 is given or mailed, whichever occurs first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inadequately identified protests may not be matched or entered; timely service on the applicant is required for entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest content requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: A protest must include: (1) an information list of documents or information with specified identification for U.S. patents, U.S. patent application publications, foreign patents/published applications, non-patent publications, and other information; (2) a concise explanation of the relevance of each item; (3) a legible copy of each item other than U.S. patents and U.S. patent application publications; (4) English translations for non-English items; and (5) if a second or subsequent protest by the same real party in interest, an explanation why the issues are significantly different and why they were not presented earlier, plus a processing fee (§ 1.17(i)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests require detailed identification, relevance explanations, and supporting copies; repeat protestors face additional hurdles and fees.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protest process limitations and consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: A protestor will not receive communications from the Office relating to the protest other than the return of a self-addressed postcard acknowledgment. The protestor's involvement ends with filing; no further submission on behalf of the protestor will be considered unless made under the conditions of paragraph (c)(5). Protests raising inequitable conduct issues that satisfy the entry provisions will be entered into the file generally without comment on the inequitable conduct issues. Applicant need not reply in the absence of an Office request. Protests failing to comply with required provisions may not be entered and may be returned or discarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protests are a one-shot submission mechanism: limited interaction, limited feedback, and strict compliance requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory invention registration request content (pre-2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: An applicant could request publication of the specification and drawings as a statutory invention registration (applicable to requests filed prior to March 16, 2013). The request had to be signed by the applicant and any assignee of record or an attorney/agent, and include: (1) a waiver of the applicant's right to receive a patent effective upon publication; (2) the required fee (§ 1.17(n) or (o)); (3) a statement that, in the requester’s opinion, the application meets the requirements of 35 U.S.C. 112; and (4) a statement that the application complies with the formal requirements for printing as a patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This option required signing, fee payment, and affirmative statements about compliance with statutory and formal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of waiver for statutory invention registration (pre-2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: A waiver filed with a request for a statutory invention registration would be effective upon publication to waive the inventor's right to receive a patent on the invention claimed effective upon the date of publication; the waiver applies to the requester's application and certain subsequent or commonly owned applications as detailed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing a statutory invention registration request carried substantive rights consequences; applicants needed to understand its legal effect.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examination of statutory invention registration request (pre-2013)
rubrics_metrics.description: Any request for a statutory invention registration would be examined to determine if the § 1.293 requirements were met and whether the application met requirements for publication (including 35 U.S.C. 112). Applicant would be notified of results and given time to comply or face abandonment; failure to meet 35 U.S.C. 112 would result in a rejection and possible final refusal of the request if not timely corrected. Reply periods were subject to extension rules of § 1.136.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requests were substantive and the Office examined both the request and the application; procedural noncompliance or substantive 112 defects could lead to final refusal.
